education.title: Biomechanics Foundations
education.summary: Forces, moments, levers, and joint loading - how movement creates stress and performance.

sections.title: Force & Torque
sections.body: Force changes motion; torque rotates joints. External torque vs internal muscle torque defines demand.

sections.title: Levers
sections.body: Most human joints operate as third-class levers - favoring speed and range over mechanical advantage.

sections.title: Ground Reaction Force
sections.body: GRF informs loading patterns. Foot placement and trunk angle shift joint moments.

education.title: Strength & Power Essentials
education.summary: Strength qualities, power production, and technique that reduces unnecessary stress.

sections.title: Strength vs Power
sections.body: Strength is force capacity; power is force * velocity. Programming targets both with intent.

sections.title: Intent & Technique
sections.body: Technique consistency enables safe intensity. Intent drives neural recruitment.

education.title: Mobility & Control
education.summary: Range of motion plus control - joint prep and stability to express movement safely.

sections.title: Mobility vs Flexibility
sections.body: Mobility is usable ROM with control; flexibility alone may not transfer to movement.

sections.title: Stability
sections.body: Stability directs force. When stability lags, compensation patterns appear.

education.title: Injury Risk Signals
education.summary: Common signals in squats, hinges, and lunges and how to correct them.

sections.title: Knee Valgus
sections.body: Often driven by hip control and foot mechanics; cue tripod foot and hip external rotation control.

sections.title: Lumbar Rounding
sections.body: May indicate hip ROM limits or bracing deficits; regress load and pattern hinge.

movements.name: Back Squat
movements.description: Compound squat pattern emphasizing knee/hip coordination and trunk stability.

movements.name: Hip Hinge
movements.description: Foundational pattern for deadlifts and swings - hip flexion with neutral spine control.

careers.title: Physical Therapist (PT)
careers.summary: Rehab, movement restoration, return-to-play planning, and patient education.

careers.title: Strength & Conditioning Coach
careers.summary: Performance programming, technique coaching, and athlete development.
